title: L0-01 · The writing system and the family of the "tooth"

blocks.text: L0-01 · The writing system and the family of the "tooth"
Lesson overview
In this lesson learn how Arabic scripture works and read and write the first five letters ( ⁧ا ب ت ث ن⁩ ) with all the short vowels: in the end you read and write ten true words.

rows: 5–7 hours · one week at a standard pace

blocks.text: Materials This unit, calligraphy notebook (Part V), Level Anki deck 0, pencil, striped notebook, phone to register
Targets. At the end of the lesson you know:
1. explain how Arabic writing works: direction, consonants and vowels, connection, forms of letters;
2. recognize, pronounce and write ⁧ا ب ت ث ن⁩ in all their forms;
3. read and write syllables with fatḥa, kasra, ḍamma, sukūn and ā long;
4. read, write and translate the ten words of the vocabulary;
5. to distinguish by ear from ṯ, b da n, soon from ā Long.
Plan of the week (60 minutes a day, of which 10–15 of Anki from the day 2).

1. How Arabic writing works

Arabic is written from right to left, in italics mandatory, marking the consonants and long vowels; short vowels are optional signs. The rest of this section explains the practical consequences of these three rules.
1.1 What Arabic You're Learning

He studies modern standard Arabic (MSA): the written language common to all Arab countries, used in newspapers, documents, news and official speeches. Next to it each country has its spoken dialects, which you will face later as a separate competence. The writing and the letters are the same for everyone.
1.2 From right to left

Each line starts on the right and continues to the left; A book opens from what is the last page for you. Words are read from the right-handest letter. The numbers are written from left to right: you will see them in L0-10.
1.3 You write consonants

The Arabic alphabet is an abjad: le 28 letters are consonant. Three of them ( ⁧ا و ي⁩ ) also serve to write long vowels ā, ū, ī. Short vowels are not letters: they are small signs above or below the consonant, called ḥarakāt. The vocal signs appear in the Koran, children's books, manuals, poetry and when a word would be ambiguous. Most of them are missing in newspapers, documents, websites and social media. That's why you learn to read vowels first and then, gradually, without. An example you will use in this lesson: the handwriting ⁧بنت⁩ "Bint' (the girl) or "banat' (the woman's name) is read. Only vowels, or context, decide.
1.4 Connected script and four letter forms
In Arabic there is no capital letters: the letters of a word join along the basic line. For this reason each letter has up to four forms, and the form depends on two questions.
The first and the last letters of the word """ are not meant to mean the beginning and end of a connected section. A word may contain several traits.
1.5 Six letters don't connect left.

The letters ⁧ا د ذ ر ز و⁩ they stick to the previous but never to the next. They therefore have only two forms, isolated and final, and after them the word starts again with a new trait, even in half a word. Today you meet the first:
Example: in ⁧بَاب⁩ ( bāb, the first ⁧ب⁩ is initial, the ⁧ا⁩ is final, and the last ⁧ب⁩ is isolated, because the ⁧ا⁩ She doesn't give her her hand and after her the word ends.
1.6 Same body, different points

Many letters share the same skeleton and are distinguished only by number and position of points. Today you study the family of the tooth: at the beginning and in the middle of the word ⁧ب ت ث ن⁩ They have the same little tooth.

In L0-02 Added ⁧ي⁩ , with two points below. Write rule: first trace the skeleton of the whole word without detaching the pen, then add points and vowels. In handwriting, two points often become a dash and three points a small "^^": recognize them, but for now write them separately.
1.7 Other characteristics
• No capitals. Names have no special marks.
• Basic line. The letters rest on an imaginary line; some forms descend below, such as the ⁧ن⁩ Final.
• The syllables always start with a consonant. Possible syllables are CV (ba), CVV (bā) and CVC
(bin); at the end of isolated word also CVVC (bāb) and CVCC (bint). The words that seem to begin with vowel actually start with a glottis stroke, the hamza, which you will study in L0-09.
1.8 Pause pronunciation

When you say a word isolated, or the last word of a sentence, the final short vowel falls. The words of the vocabulary are given in this paul form: ⁧بَاب⁩ = bāb. Complete terminations (bābun, bāban, bābin) will arrive in L0-09 and A1-19. Verbs are quoted with the final vowel, as in dictionaries: ⁧ثَبَتَ⁩ = ṯabata; at the end of a sentence it is pronounced ṯabat.
1.9 The accent

In MSA the emphasis does not distinguish different words and varies a little from region to region. Practical rule: if the last syllable has a long vowel followed by consonant (-āt, -āb, -ān) takes the accent (ba- nāt , na- bāt ); otherwise falls on the previous syllable ( ṯā -bit). A shifted accent does not change the meaning: the length of the vowels does.
2. Short vowels, sukūn and long ā
The standard Arabic has only three vocal stamps, a, i, u, each short or long; length changes the meaning of words.
⁧بَا⁩ fatḥa + alif bā /aː/ fatḥa on the consonant, then ⁧ا⁩
The names of the signs are written with letters that you don't know yet: for now you just need to recognize the sign.
2.1 How to pronounce them
• fatḥa /a/. After today's letters it sounds clear, between the a of the house and the open one of the bene ([a]~[æ]). Near
Ethical consonants (L0-06) becomes darker, [ɑ].
• kasra /i/. One i, sometimes just more open [ ɪ ]. Do not turn it into e: bint, non-bent.
• ḍamma /u/. One u, sometimes just more open [ʊ]. Don't turn it into o.
• sukūn. The consonant remains without vowel and closes the syllable. In ⁧بِنْت⁩ (bint) the n and t final are pronounced
dry, without the support that in English would be spontaneous.
2.2 The length is a phoneme

A long vowel lasts about twice the short vowel. In Italian the duration of the vowels does not distinguish words (the double consonants do it: "fato" / "facto"), so your ear is not trained to notice it. In Arabic yes: banat banāt The girls differ only for the length of the second a. Train yourself exaggerating at the beginning: bā as if it were "baa" (baa) " . The ā long is written with fatḥa on the consonant followed by ⁧ا⁩ . Many texts omit the fatḥa before ⁧ا⁩ , because it's obvious; You write it all the way through the Level. 0.

3. The five letters

Four letters share the tooth ( ⁧ب ت ث ن⁩ ) and one, ⁧ا⁩ , marks ā long and does not connect to the next. The shapes are read from right to left inside each cell; the indent ⁧ـ⁩ ( taṭwīl) indicates which side of the letter is linked.
⁧ن⁩ nūn ( ⁧نُون⁩ ) n /n/ ⁧ن⁩ ⁧نـ⁩ ⁧ـنـنـ⁩
3.1 ⁧ب⁩ · bāʾ
• Sound. /b/, sound bilabial occlusive: lips closed, then release, with vocal cords vibrating. It's the b
Italian di .
• Tracked. Isolated and final: start from the right with a small hook upwards, go down to the line, swipe towards
left and close with a short ascent; Then the bottom point, in the middle. Initial and median: only the tooth, which joins the line to the left.
• Examples ⁧بَاب⁩ bāb "Door" (initial and isolated) · ⁧بِنْت⁩ bint
• Typical error. Point forgotten or put on: at the beginning of the word the letter becomes ⁧ن⁩ .
3.2 ⁧ت⁩ · tāʾ
• Sound. /t/, occlusive deaf dental, non-emphasising: tip of the tongue against the back of the upper incisors,
without suction. It is the Italian t of .
• Tracked. Same body as ⁧ب⁩ ; two points above (by hand, often a dash).
• Examples ⁧تِبْن⁩ tibn (initial) "paglia" ⁧بِنْت⁩ bint (final).
• Typical error. Confuse it with ⁧ث⁩ I'm not counting the points. In L0-07 meet you ⁧ط⁩ , the emphasis: keep ⁧ت⁩
Lightweight, with relaxed tongue.
3.3 ⁧ث⁩ · ṯāʾ
• Sound. /θ/, deaf fricativa: tip of the tongue between incisors (or just behind the edge of
upper), air blows without vibrate the vocal cords. In Italian, it does not exist: it is the sound of English and Spanish from Castigliano to Cinco.
• Tracked. Same body as ⁧ب⁩ ; three points above triangle (by hand, often a small
• Examples ⁧ثَابِت⁩ ṯābit "Stable" (initial) · ⁧ثَبَات⁩ ṯabāt :Stablety.
• Typical error. Pronouncing it t, s or f. Change the word: ⁧تَابَ⁩ tāba “repented” ≠ ⁧ثَابَ⁩ ṯāba He's back to himself.
• Note on dialects. In Egypt and the Levant ⁧ث⁩ often becomes t o s ( ⁧ثَلَاثَة⁩ • three • → talāta). In MSA
stays /θ/.
3.4 ⁧ن⁩ · nūn
• Sound. /n/, alveolar nasal: tip of the tongue on the gums behind the upper incisors, air from the nose. It is the n
Italian.
• Tracked. Isolated and final: a rounder and deeper cup of ⁧ب⁩ , which comes down below the line, with the point
above the center. Initial and median: a tooth identical to that of ⁧ب⁩ , with one point above.
• Examples ⁧نَبَات⁩ nabāt (initial) plant · ⁧بِنْت⁩ bint (medial) · ⁧تِبْن⁩ tibn (final).
• Typical error. In the beginning or in the middle, confuse it with ⁧ب⁩ or ⁧ت⁩ : Counts and locates points. At the end of the day,
write it flat as ⁧ب⁩ .
3.5 ⁧ا⁩ · alif
• Function today. After a consonant with fatḥa marks the ā Long. Alone has no consonant sound; a
start word brings a hamza ( ⁧أ⁩ ), which you will see in L0-09.
• Sound. [aː): after ⁧ب ت ث ن⁩ is clear and open; close to the stress becomes darker [ɑː].
• Forms. Only isolated ⁧ا⁩ and final ⁧ـا⁩ : never connects to the next letter.
• Tracked. A vertical stretch from top to bottom. If connected to the right, start from the line and go up.
• Examples ⁧بَاب⁩ bāb · ⁧بَنَات⁩ banāt: after ⁧ا⁩ the ⁧ت⁩ It starts again, and being the last letter is isolated.
• Typical error. Unite ⁧ا⁩ in the following letter, or read it as a short voice.
3.6 Minimum pairs
A minimal pair are two words that differ for one sound: it is proof that that sound distinguishes meanings.

The root is the group of (usually) three consonants that bears the basic meaning; the patterns of vowels and affixes build words. You already see a family today: ⁧ث ب ت⁩ gives ⁧ثَبَتَ⁩ (b) be settled, established, ⁧ثَابِت⁩ • balance, fixed, ⁧ثَبَات⁩ “steadfastness”. It is the central mechanism of language (A2-01 and B1-01). The root of ⁧بِنْت⁩ is traditionally ⁧ب ن و⁩ ; some dictionaries report it below ⁧ب ن ي⁩ . The plurals in the table are information to be recognized, not to be memorized now.

6. Listening and speaking

This lesson does not contain audio files: I give you ready scripts for an Arabic speech synthesis and I'll tell you how to verify them with native speakers. At this stage \'listening Â" means to distinguish sounds and write under dictation; the understanding of dialogues begins in A1-01.
6.1 How to use speech synthesis
• Tools. An Arabic voice of an online translator (with the speaker button), or reading to
voice of the phone (on iPhone: Settings › Accessibility › Content read aloud, with an Arabic voice downloaded).
• Limits. Synthetic vowels often ignore vocal signs, read isolated syllables as letters names,
add desinence or use a regional pronunciation (some Egyptian voices make ⁧ث⁩ as t o s). Use them to train your ear, not as a pronunciation pattern.
• Check with native speakers. Search for words on Forvo, the dictionary of pronunciations recorded by native speakers
(not all words are present), and from A1 Have a tutor check your pronunciation.
